section: RMIT University case study: results from Symphony auto-detection, call statistics and reporting
body:
This part of the RMIT University case study describes what changed after the university added AVI-SPL's Symphony platform: how tickets are raised, how faults are found, and how video conferencing quality problems were solved. It is useful as proof of the operational effect of proactive monitoring.

**Results as stated**

- Client-initiated tickets have gone down while auto-detected tickets have gone up. Auto-detection is based on thresholds that RMIT defined.
- Symphony is driving down the mean time to resolution (MTTR), which the page links to a more reliable, high-quality teaching and learning experience for faculty and students.
- Expected over time, not yet claimed as achieved: auto-detection will enable the AV and IT support resources to lower their field support personnel requirements and costs, by giving data-driven guidance on the health of the estate.
- Tim Sullivan, RMIT senior manager of operations for learning, teaching and research, said that since the implementation the audio-visual services team has become more efficient and has improved the student and staff experience.

**Examples given**

- **Faulty power supplies.** Through Symphony service thresholds, the AV support team was alerted to a device that kept going on and offline through the night. On investigating the location, the team found a faulty power supply unit (PSU). Further analysis showed that a number of these PSUs were faulty, and the team replaced them proactively.
- **Video call quality between Vietnam and Melbourne.** Because Symphony monitors AV and video conferencing devices, it resolved longstanding video conferencing quality issues. Live monitoring and call statistics showed network speed dropping gradually during calls between the two cities. Using the live data together with historical call statistics, RMIT narrowed down which settings to adjust to make calls more reliable and better in quality. The AV support teams in the different countries were able to fix the issue.

**Business intelligence**

Data from Symphony's reports and analytics helps guide decisions on which technologies may be due for an upgrade, optimizes internal business processes once thresholds are reached, and shows trends over time.

**When to use this**

Use it when a customer asks what measurable or practical difference Symphony made for a real organization, how auto-detected tickets work in practice, or whether monitoring can help diagnose video call quality.

**Not stated in this source:** ticket volumes, MTTR figures, cost savings or percentages for these results.
